question: A 25-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after he was involved in a motorcycle collision. He was not wearing a helmet. Physical examination shows left periorbital ecchymosis. A CT scan of the head shows a fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone with compression of the left superior orbital fissure. Physical examination of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?

options.ope: Complete loss of vision of the left eye

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone" -> "Compression of the left superior orbital fissure" -> "Potential damage to cranial nerves III, IV, VI, and V1" -> "Possible absent left corneal reflex due to V1 involvement" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone" -> "Compression of the left superior orbital fissure" -> "Involvement of the oculomotor nerve (CN III)" -> "Possible ptosis and pupillary involvement" -> "Absent left corneal reflex due to sensory loss" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone" -> "Compression of the left superior orbital fissure" -> "Involvement of the abducens nerve (CN VI)" -> "Possible impaired lateral gaze on the left" -> "Not preserved left lateral gaze" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone" -> "Compression of the left superior orbital fissure" -> "Involvement of the maxillary nerve (V2)" -> "Possible numbness of the left cheek" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone" -> "Compression of the left superior orbital fissure" -> "Involvement of the optic nerve (CN II)" -> "Possible complete loss of vision of the left eye" -> 60%
analysis: The patient has a fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone with compression of the left superior orbital fissure. This can lead to damage to cranial nerves that pass through the superior orbital fissure, particularly the oculomotor nerve (CN III), trochlear nerve (CN IV), abducens nerve (CN VI), and the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve (CN V1). The absent left corneal reflex indicates involvement of the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve, which is responsible for the sensory component of the reflex. Therefore, the most likely finding on examination is an absent left corneal reflex.
